newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money firm on C Bank rate.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money firm on C Bank rate.

text.p: *Volume lower at 14.26 bln pesos from 14.37 bln
Manila overnight money stayed at an average of 20.03125 percent on Wednesday after the Central Bank left unchanged its overnight borrowing rate at 20 percent, traders said.
The market had expected a cut in the rate after the U.S. Federal Reserve decided not to change its rates.
Last Thursday and Friday, the Central Bank raised its key rate several times to defend the peso from speculation.
Done rates were at a lower range of 20.25 percent to 20.03125. The market had 31 lenders and 16 borrowers.
On the secondary market, some banks continued to buy bills in anticipation of an eventual rate cut, traders said.
Banks particularly wanted to get hold of one-year bills.

"But the market view is mixed since the overnight rate is still at 20 percent," a dealer said. The Central Bank may extend its overnight borrowing rate at 20 percent for another week until speculation fully dies down, he added.
A Reuters poll of five financial institutions gave bid rates of 10.95/11.15 percent for the three-month bills; 11.50/11.75 for the six months; and 12 to 12.25 for the one-year bills.
